audited: a READ-ONLY unit-bearing surface, and every figure it renders is resolved through the reader's adapters. Tread through u.tread (the table cell via `format`, the chart series via `toDisplay` with the Y axis labelled from `u.tread.label`, so the plotted numbers and the axis unit come from ONE adapter and cannot disagree). Distance, known distance and the wear projection through u.distance.format. There are no entry fields and therefore no origins to preserve: nothing here is submitted. It recomputes no distance or projection either -- both arrive already computed by TireService, the same values the tire card renders, so the two surfaces cannot drift. The prompts, the readiness counts and the series colours name no unit; the counts are dimensionless. Re-reviewed after the data fetch moved from react-query to the useEffect + api.get shape the rest of Analytics.tsx uses. That changed how the payload ARRIVES and nothing about how any figure is resolved: the same adapters format the same canonical fields.

tread and pressure through useUnitFormat with seeded origins. Phase 5a made the reading drawer's tread OPTIONAL (#152): the at-least-one guard now resolves BOTH tread and pressure through canonicalFromUnitField before refusing, where it resolved tread alone and left pressure to be converted inside the payload literal. That is the same unit decision applied to a second field, not a new one, and both still submit the seeded canonical value when untouched. A pressure-only reading posts tread_depth_mm: null, which carries no unit; the card already guarded its tread cell with `!= null` because Tire.tread_depth_mm was nullable already. The reading-history drawer added after phase 5a renders tread, pressure and odometer through u.tread / u.pressure / u.distance, the same three adapters and the same resolved `u` the card above it uses, so a history row cannot disagree with the card. It reads canonical fields only through `num()` and formats every one of them; nothing raw reaches the DOM, and a mutation swapping the tread cell for String(reading.tread_depth_mm) fails TireList.test.tsx. The overlay button that opens it carries no unit. The rotate and retire drawers added when the three unreachable flows got a UI introduce two more DISTANCE entry fields, and both take the same route as the mount and dismount ones: an empty origin (they open blank, so there is no seeded canonical to preserve), submission through canonicalFromUnitField(..., u.distance), and a label from `odometerWithUnit` interpolating u.distance.label rather than naming a unit. All FOUR odometer inputs now carry step={u.distance.step}; only the reading drawer's did, and the other three fell back to the HTML default of 1. That default happens to equal u.distance.step for every distance unit in the vocabulary, both of which are whole-unit, so this is a guard against a future decimal distance unit rather than a behaviour change today. The rotation pattern chips, the move preview (two position labels per row) and the storage chip carry no unit and no number. Tire sets add exactly ONE unit-bearing control: the per-set fit odometer (`set-fit-odometer-{id}`), which takes the same route as the other four -- empty origin, `canonicalFromUnitField(..., u.distance)`, the shared `odometerWithUnit` label, `step={u.distance.step}`. Everything else the sets work introduced is dimensionless: `setMembership` interpolates two COUNTS (`Tires: {{total}} · Fitted: {{mounted}}`), the set name is free text, the membership chips carry names, and the stored-tire grouping only reorders cards whose unit-bearing cells were already dispositioned above. Re-reviewed for v3.4.0's mount-history UI (six commits since v3.3.1, ~494 changed lines): the new mountedLine/storedLine card lines format through u.distance.format like every other card field; every MountEventFields odometer field in Add-to-corner, Mount, Dismount and Retire submits through canonicalFromUnitField(...,u.distance), the same route the pre-existing rotate/retire/fit odometers already used; storage_location is free text with no unit; the retired-tire cards reuse the same tread/distanceSummary adapters already audited above; restore is dimensionless. No new unit decision was introduced -- the existing contract was extended to five more call sites. Re-reviewed for the v3.4.0 review fixes: Mount, Dismount, Retire and Rotate now reset their date and odometer when the dialog OPENS rather than on success, to the same EMPTY_ODOMETER (empty origin) they were already reset to, so every submission still goes through canonicalFromUnitField(..., u.distance) from an empty origin; and storage_location, free text with no unit, is now sent only on the branches that render its input. the admin writer for the instance-wide `default_unit_prefs` row, added by phase 4 task 5 under ruling R5. It exists because retiring the `imperial_gallon_standard` control with nothing in its place is D5's own failure mode moved from users to instances: that control was the only lever an admin had on what anonymous visitors and every client on an `auth_mode=none` instance render, and the row it fed also seeds every new account (`new_user_unit_kwargs`) and every `auth_mode=none` PDF and notification (`render_context_default`). NO UNIT DECISION IS MADE HERE and no `units-exempt` pragma is claimed: the eleven controls are `components/settings/UnitSetEditor.tsx`, reused rather than reimplemented, so the vocabulary, the option labels, the D3 confirmation and the R4 UK-gallon warning are all the shared ones; `presetTagFor` decides the highlight from the published set, and `basePresetFor` expands a preset exactly as the account writer does. Three decisions carry weight. (1) The gate is `isAdmin || authMode === 'none'`, never `isAdmin` alone: in `auth_mode=none` the backend allows settings administration and returns no user, so the frontend reports `isAdmin === false` for precisely the population this control exists for. (2) The write is `POST /settings/batch`, which upserts, and not `PUT /settings/{key}`, which 404s on a missing row: an instance whose row was deleted through the generic `DELETE /api/settings/{key}` is the case the backend fallback exists for and the batch route is the one that can recover it. The body is the full eleven-field set as a JSON STRING under the settings key, matching what both backend writers store. (3) The write calls `refreshUser()`, which re-reads `/settings/public`, because `defaultUnitPrefs` is React state populated only inside `AuthContext.loadUser` and nothing else re-reads it: without that call every mounted consumer keeps rendering the old default until the page is reloaded. `components/settings/__tests__/InstanceUnitDefaultsCard.test.tsx` mounts the REAL `AuthProvider` and a separate `useUnitPreference` probe, so the card's own optimistic state cannot satisfy the live-apply case; both the gate and the refresh were proved by deliberate mutation. FIX ROUND AFTER TASK 5 added a FOURTH weighted decision: the card renders nothing until `publicSettingsLoaded` is true. Decision (1)'s gate is read off `/settings/public` and so is the row this card writes, so before that request resolves once, every input to both is an initial value rather than an answer: `authMode` starts at 'none', which leaves the gate open, and `defaultUnitPrefs` starts null, which the display fallback turns into the imperial preset. `components/settings/UnitSetEditor.tsx` gives the two PRESET buttons a confirmation and the Custom button none, so on a UK or metric `auth_mode=none` instance whose boot fetch failed, an admin opening the per-quantity grid would write US imperial as the instance-wide default for everyone, permanently, having chosen nothing. The new case in the card's test rejects `/settings/public` and asserts the card's absence after the provider settles; removing the guard fails it. Re-reviewed for v3.4.0 task 11: `applySelection` now calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['tires'] })` immediately after `refreshUser()`, because `history_faults[].message` is worded by the server in the caller's distance unit and the tire list query is cached for the app's 30-second staleTime -- without this, a mounted tire card would keep showing the previous default's sentence after this row changes it. The call is a cache-invalidation side effect over an opaque query key array; it renders nothing and converts no quantity itself. No unit decision. 2026-09-23 (cleanup): its admin gate is now useCanManageInstance (same rule, isAdmin || authMode none). No unit logic touched.

the account and browser writers for unit preferences, and the only place either is written. It repairs two live regressions: `PUT /auth/me` with a `unit_preference` key (a 422 since D9b removed the field, which the frontend suite could not see because `@/services/api` is mocked) and the anonymous branch's legacy localStorage writes (which `unitPrefsStore` ignores once its own key exists). Three unit decisions live here and each is deliberate. (1) The HIGHLIGHT reads the client's RECORDED preference and the sentence under it reads the RESOLVED set, so an account tagged with a preset while resolving to something else shows that disagreement instead of being quietly relabelled, and the highlighted button is the lever that repairs it. Nothing on the write path takes a same-value early return, in either of the two spellings a reviewer would reach for. (2) `unitsBodyFor` sends a preset with the show-both toggle ONLY when the resolved set IS that preset, and otherwise materialises what the account already resolves to: the route writes eleven nulls for any preset, so echoing a stale tag would delete a user's units as a side effect of a display toggle. (3) The anonymous show-both write keeps `units` as the store already holds it, INCLUDING null, because writing the resolved set there would invent an explicit browser choice that outranks `default_unit_prefs` forever. The gallon panel and the composed show-both example moved here unchanged from `SettingsSystemTab.tsx`; the panel now reads the gallon store rather than a local copy of the admin-only `/settings` response. Task 4's review, MAJOR: the anonymous show-both branch used to pass `storedPrefs?.units` into `setUnitPrefs`, which persisted a migration-derived set and froze the unchosen gallon flavour permanently, reaching `a704a5b`'s own twenty percent defect through a different door. It now calls `setShowBothUnits(next)` and passes no set at all. The boundary is the fix: the card holds a set but cannot know whether it was CHOSEN or merely derived for this session, so the store owns that decision. Phase 4 task 5 DELETED the gallon panel from this card, and with it the last `units-exempt(compare)` pragma it carried (the panel's visibility test, `binarySystemFor(editorUnits.volume) === 'imperial'`), the `gallonStandardSaving` state, the `handleGallonStandardChange` handler that wrote `imperial_gallon_standard` through `POST /settings/batch`, and the four `gallonStandardStore` imports. The panel wrote an INSTANCE-wide setting from a card whose every other control writes THIS CLIENT's units, which is why it was the one control here a non-admin could not save; `src/components/settings/InstanceUnitDefaultsCard.tsx` writes the whole `default_unit_prefs` set instead, gated on `isAdmin || authMode === 'none'`. The card's root is now a `<section aria-label>` because the settings screen carries two unit editors with deliberately identical controls and a reader has to be able to say which one is which. `utils/__tests__/unitsBinaryApiSurface.test.ts` records this file leaving the PRAGMA_SUPPRESSED list. FIX ROUND AFTER TASK 5: the anonymous HIGHLIGHT no longer reads the store's derived tag for a MIGRATED record. Rung 2 stopped rendering the migrated set verbatim (it keeps the binary system and takes the gallon flavour from the instance), so the stored tag names a set this client does not render: a browser holding legacy `imperial` plus a stale `us` cache on a UK instance would have highlighted Imperial over `editorUnits` reading gal_uk, with the Custom grid hidden, which is decision (1) above inverted and the exact dishonesty migration 093 fixed server-side. A migrated record now falls through to `presetTagFor(resolvedUnits)`, the honest label for the set actually on screen; an account's own `unit_preference` and a CHOSEN browser record are untouched. Two cases in `components/settings/__tests__/UnitPreferencesCard.test.tsx` pin both directions, and deleting the guard fails the migrated one. The anonymous branches are untouched -- they write only to local storage, which the server-formatted message does not read. rows.reason: the Imperial / Metric / Custom control and the eleven per-quantity selects, extracted as a WRITER-AGNOSTIC component: it holds no state, makes no request and knows nothing about accounts. Before it there was no reusable editor at all, only one monolithic block inside `SettingsSystemTab`, so the instance-default settings row would have had to write a second set of eleven controls and a second answer to every question below. Three unit decisions. (1) `UnitSetSelection` is a UNION that mirrors `UnitPreferenceUpdate.units_present_exactly_when_custom`, so a caller cannot express a preset carrying units or a custom carrying none. (2) The eleven controls are derived from `UNIT_FIELD_NAMES` and `unitOptionsFor`, never listed, and `secondary_gallon` is among them with show-both OFF (D4b: the widget endpoints always emit MPG and something has to say which gallon that MPG means). (3) Choosing a preset CLEARS every override column, so the confirmation precedes the write and lives HERE rather than in the writer, because both writers clear identically and a confirmation the second one forgot would be invisible; it names the US-gallon consequence when the client's set currently means UK gallons (R4). The one `units-exempt(compare)` pragma is on that warning's own line and is kind-scoped. The two preset label keys sit on `labelKey` FIELDS rather than in a `Record<Preset, string>`, because `validate-i18n-usage.ts` reads a bare literal argument and a module-level string const and sees neither a record lookup nor, given the vitest mock returns the key unchanged, a component test failing on a missing one: the pair would have been outside every i18n gate this repo has. New in v3.4.0: records a closed mount period the tire spent on a corner in the past, a sibling of MountPeriodEditor.tsx for a create rather than an edit. Both odometer fields start at EMPTY_ODOMETER (no canonical origin to preserve, since there is no existing period to seed from) and are submitted through canonicalFromUnitField(mountedOdometer.typed, mountedOdometer.origin, u.distance) and the same call for dismountedOdometer, the identical seed-then-canonicalize contract MountPeriodEditor.tsx and the rest of TireList.tsx already use. Both MountEventFields instances receive odometerLabel from the shared odometerWithUnit interpolation, so the label composes u.distance.label rather than naming a unit itself; the nearest-reading suggestion and its Use control are MountEventFields' own concern, already audited on that file's row. The corner picker renders five Chips labelled through the caller's labelFor, a position string with no unit. Dates and notes are dimensionless; notes is sent trimmed-or-null like every other free-text field in this feature.

New in v3.4.0: the shared date-and-odometer field pair used by every tire operation. The odometer input carries step={u.distance.step} and is stored as {typed, origin}; onOdometerChange forwards the typed string and origin unchanged, so conversion happens at the caller's canonicalFromUnitField(...,u.distance) on submit, the same contract the four odometer fields already audited in TireList.tsx use. The nearest-reading suggestion is unit-bearing directly: it formats the fetched canonical odometer_km through u.distance.format(Number(reading.odometer_km)), and accepting it (Use) seeds the field through seedUnitField(Number(reading.odometer_km), u.distance) rather than re-parsing the rounded display string, which is the exact bug the file's own docstring says the branch's last commit corrected. offset()/suggestionSameDay/suggestionEarlier/suggestionLater name a day count, not a unit. No raw number reaches the DOM outside these two adapter calls.

New in v3.4.0: corrects one mount period's dates, odometers and notes. Both odometer fields are seeded on open through seedUnitField(num(period.mounted_odometer_km), u.distance) and seedUnitField(num(period.dismounted_odometer_km), u.distance), and submitted through canonicalFromUnitField(...,u.distance) for both mounted_odometer_km and dismounted_odometer_km, the same seed-then-canonicalize contract MountEventFields and the rest of TireList.tsx already use. The odometer label is the shared odometerWithUnit interpolation. Dates and notes are dimensionless. The dismount pair renders, and is only sent, when the period is already closed, matching the server contract described in the file's own docstring.

New in v3.4.0, split out of TireList.tsx: renders a tire's mount periods and readings. The odometer() helper formats every mount/dismount bound through u.distance.format(num(v)), used for the period list, the periodSince/periodRange rows and the firstInstalled line; readings render tread, pressure and odometer through u.tread.format/u.pressure.format/u.distance.format, the identical three adapters TireList.tsx's own reading history already used before this file was split out. needsOdometer() and the Assumed/Needs an odometer/Check this period badges are booleans and text, not unit-bearing. No raw canonical value reaches the DOM outside the odometer()/tread/pressure adapter calls. Re-reviewed for reading delete: each reading row gains a Delete button whose label is common:delete, whose aria-label and native confirm interpolate the reading's date through formatDateForDisplay, and whose click sends { tireId, readingId } to useDeleteTireReading. Ids and a date, no quantity. The toasts are readingDeleted and getActionErrorMessage over readingDeleteAction, neither of which names a unit. The tread, pressure and odometer cells on the row still render only through u.tread.format / u.pressure.format / u.distance.format. ` row renders `fault.message` verbatim -- free text the server has already formatted in the caller's distance unit, exactly the same pattern as `period.notes` already dispositioned above. Fix round 1 corrected the rationale above the `subscribeToConverterGallon` subscription: it still said every consumption and fuel-rate reader takes the binary system and reads `UnitConverter`'s mutable statics, which task 6b made false for all of them. Task 8 then DELETED that subscription, with `hooks/useResolvedGallonSync.ts`, the three converter-gallon exports in `utils/units.ts` and the `App` provider call: a sync that wrote process-global factors no screen reads, published to one subscriber that discarded the value. `gallonStandard` here is resolved per rung and never came from the converter, so no behaviour moved. What still writes those factors is `gallonStandardStore`, and `utils/__tests__/unitsBinaryApiSurface.test.ts` now enumerates the eight methods that touch them and holds the caller count at one. Phase 4 task 3 replaced rung 2: the hook no longer parses the legacy `unit_preference` key during render and no longer reads `show_both_units` from localStorage. Both come from `utils/unitPrefsStore.ts`, subscribed through `useSyncExternalStore`, so a client with no account can hold a full per-quantity set instead of one bit, and rung 2 collapses `system` and `gallonStandard` FROM that set the way rungs 1 and 3 already did rather than expanding a preset. `readStoredUnitSystem` is deleted and its `units-exempt(compare)` pragma moved to the store with the read it excuses. The file header's four-rung comment was rewritten rather than appended to, because rung 2 is no longer 'the key being PRESENT'. Phase 4 task 5 removed the SECOND subscription this file held: the `gallonStandardStore` one, which supplied `cachedGallonStandard` to exactly two positions, rung 1's stale-bundle fallback and rung 4. Both now read `defaultUnitPrefs ?? basePresetFor('imperial')` through one `fallbackUnits` / `fallbackGallon` pair, so the instance-wide answer arrives as an eleven-quantity set from `/settings/public` rather than as one bit cached in `localStorage` under `imperial_gallon_standard`. The sentence above about `gallonStandardStore` still writing the mutable converter factors is history now: the store is deleted and that enumeration reads `[]`. ONE THING IS LOST AND IT IS STATED IN THE FILE: the cached key survived a failed `/settings/public`, so a UK instance whose boot fetch failed still rendered UK gallons; nothing caches the published set, so such a client falls to the imperial preset for that session and heals on the next successful load. That is the same degradation `parse_default_unit_prefs` applies server-side for an unreadable row, it is transient rather than the permanent freeze commits a704a5b and f3b86e5 removed. THE CLAIM THAT RUNG 1 (every authenticated client) IS UNAFFECTED WAS FALSE and the fix round corrected it in the file: `AuthContext.loadUser` awaits `/settings/public` BEFORE `/auth/me`, so on that failure there are no rung-1 clients at all, everybody drops to rung 4 and gets `basePresetFor('imperial')`. Rung 1 is untouched only when the fetch SUCCEEDS and the row is missing or unparseable, and 'for the session' means until the tab reloads, which on an installed PWA can be days. FIX ROUND AFTER TASK 5, MAJOR: RUNG 2 NO LONGER HANDS A MIGRATED SET'S GALLON FLAVOUR THROUGH. `utils/unitPrefsStore.ts::migrateLegacy` builds its set from `localStorage['imperial_gallon_standard']`, which was never a browser choice but a cache of an instance value written by `useGallonStandardSync`; task 5 deleted that writer, so the key can no longer heal and a stale one made every volume, price per volume and MPG about twenty percent wrong for that browser forever. This is `a704a5b` and `f3b86e5`'s defect reached by freezing the INPUT instead of the record. For a record the store flags `units_are_migrated`, rung 2 now keeps only the binary system the browser actually chose and expands it through `presetUnitsFor` with the flavour of the LIVE `default_unit_prefs`; the dead cache's word survives only when the instance publishes no default at all, which is the failed-fetch client and the same value it rendered before the upgrade. A set written through `setUnitPrefs` is not flagged and is handed through untouched, because that is a real per-quantity choice and is why rung 2 outranks rung 3. `hooks/__tests__/useUnitPreference.precedence.test.tsx` carries the regression in both directions plus the two over-application guards (a CHOSEN set keeps its flavour; a migrated one keeps the cache when nothing is published), each proved by mutation. 2026-09-23 (cleanup): comment only (units are set in Quick Settings). 2026-09-24 (#172 per-vehicle distance unit): the four-rung body is now useAccountUnitPreference; useUnitPreference lays the enclosing VehicleUnitScope's odometer unit on distance and speed (unitsForVehicle), same object when there is none. system and gallonStandard are untouched. NEW 2026-09-21. One shared cache of Intl.NumberFormat instances, extracted from a private helper in unitFormat.ts so units.ts and formatUtils.ts can use it too; it imports nothing, because unitFormat -> unitAdapters -> units means any of them reaching back into unitFormat would close a cycle. Audited rather than 'no unit behaviour' on one point: it holds no unit and performs no conversion, but a wrong CACHE KEY would render a unit at another unit's precision, which is a unit defect reached through a formatting cache. Two keys exist. cachedNumberFormat takes the key from its caller (locale plus precision, for formatAtPrecision) so no serialization runs on the hot path. cachedCurrencyFormat derives its own key from the locale, currency and digits it also builds the options from, which is what makes a key/options disagreement unrepresentable for the three currency call sites; two of them had independently landed on 'locale|cost|currency' while reading their precision from separate constants. The locale is in every key because getActiveLocale() changes when the reader picks a language. Callers that want a FRAGMENT of a formatter rather than the formatter (currency.getCurrencySymbol, decimalInput.localeDecimalSeparator) correctly cache the fragment instead and do not use this module. 2026-09-30 (money-fits B7): cachedCurrencyFormat also takes CURRENCY_DIGITS, which leaves the fraction digits to Intl (yen 0, dollars 2). The mode is in the key as the digits value, so a plain amount and a fixed-precision rate in the same currency still get separate formatters; formatUtils.test.ts formats a yen amount on both sides of a yen rate to pin that. holds this browser's own unit preferences: the resolved set, the show-both modifier, and a DERIVED `unit_preference` tag. Three unit decisions live here and each is deliberate. (1) The one-shot migration expands the legacy `unit_preference` key through `presetUnitsFor` with the legacy `imperial_gallon_standard` flavour, which is the same expansion `useUnitPreference` rung 2 did inline before this task, and it computes that record for the SESSION WITHOUT PERSISTING IT. The non-persistence is the decision, not an omission. `migrateLegacy` runs at module load, which is before `useGallonStandardSync`'s `/settings/public` fetch resolves, and an absent gallon key falls back to `us`; persisting that guess froze it, because every later path is guarded on `unit_prefs` being ABSENT and `setGallonStandard` notifies only its own listeners, so nothing could heal the record. That was reachable on a UK instance whose first post-upgrade settings fetch fails (the key is never written on US instances, so its absence is indistinguishable from normal) and on any instance whose admin later switches the published flavour, and it left every volume and MPG about twenty percent wrong permanently. Not persisting keeps the legacy keys authoritative until the client makes a real choice through `setUnitPrefs`, which does persist. THAT SENTENCE USED TO END 'so rung 2 still follows the server the way it did before the store existed', and the fix round after task 5 corrected it: rung 2 followed the server only because `useGallonStandardSync` rewrote `imperial_gallon_standard` from `/settings/public` on every boot, and task 5 deleted that writer. With no writer left the key is frozen, so re-deriving each boot re-derives the same wrong answer forever: the record stopped being frozen and its INPUT stayed frozen. Closing it needs the live instance default, which this module cannot see, so the record now carries the flag and `useUnitPreference` rung 2 acts on it (see below). The claim this sentence used to make, that no browser's rendered units move, was false for exactly that population and the persist was pinned by no test at all: deleting it broke zero. `utils/__tests__/unitPrefsStore.test.ts` now fails when it is restored. When task 5 retires the legacy keys it must write the record through `setUnitPrefs` rather than assume the migration left one behind. (2) `presetTagFor` (MOVED to `types/units.ts` by phase 4 task 4, because the settings card needs the identical rule and a second copy of it is how this workstream started) names a set `custom` unless it is exactly the preset for its binary system, which is migration 093's `_materialise_uk_imperial_users` rule stated generally: the imperial and metric presets are both written with `secondary_gallon='us'`, so a UK-gallon browser is custom whichever preset it started from. Deriving the tag rather than storing it means the settings card cannot highlight a preset over a set that is not it. (3) `readLegacySystem` carries the `units-exempt(compare)` pragma that used to sit in `hooks/useUnitPreference.ts::readStoredUnitSystem`; it moved with the read it excuses and the suppression count is unchanged, which `utils/__tests__/unitsBinaryApiSurface.test.ts` pins by exact list. Token validation is `coerceUnitSet` from `types/units.ts`, so the store degrades WHOLE like the backend rather than patching a partial set from a preset. Task 4 also corrected this file's header count of the synthetic `storage` events `SettingsSystemTab` fires: it said three, and task 4 removed the two unit handlers, so the time-format handler is the only one left. The lenience the header argues for is unchanged; only the number was stale, and a stale number is what this phase keeps finding. Task 4's review found the SECOND DOOR onto the same defect and it is closed here: withholding the set inside `migrateLegacy` is not sufficient, because a later modifier-only write that persisted `current.units` froze the same module-load gallon guess as a side effect of a DISPLAY DENSITY toggle. So the store holds THREE states, not two: no units, units held FOR THIS SESSION because `migrateLegacy` derived them, and units CHOSEN through `setUnitPrefs`. Only the third may be persisted. `units_are_migrated` carries the distinction, `setShowBothUnits` is the modifier-only writer that respects it (persisting `units: null` for a migration-derived set while writing the modifier down), and `readPersisted` re-derives the set for the session when it reads a record holding modifiers but no units, which costs a browser that genuinely never chose nothing because `migrateLegacy` returns null for it. The card must not pass a set through for a modifier write: it cannot know the provenance of the set it holds. Both directions are pinned, and the state count is the point: two of these states are visible in the TYPE (`UnitSet | null`) and the third is only visible in the BEHAVIOUR, which is why enumerating from the type missed it. Phase 4 task 5 changed no behaviour in this file and corrected four claims in it that task 5 falsified. `useGallonStandardSync` is deleted, so `imperial_gallon_standard` is no longer rewritten from the server on every boot: all three legacy keys are write-once history now. That makes a presence-guarded migration merely wrong rather than catastrophic, and the ABSENCE guard on `unit_prefs` is the correct rule either way and did not move. `migrateLegacy` still reads the raw legacy key at module load and still DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PERSIST what it derives, which is the invariant commits a704a5b and f3b86e5 exist for and which task 5 deliberately did not touch: an absent gallon key still falls back to `us`, and persisting that guess would still freeze it because every later path is guarded on `unit_prefs` being absent. The three-state model (no units; units held for the session; units chosen) is unchanged. FIX ROUND AFTER TASK 5, MAJOR, and it is the THIRD DOOR onto one defect: the flag that was a module-level `let` is now a FIELD ON THE HELD RECORD (`StoredUnitPrefs extends UnitPrefsChoice` with `units_are_migrated`), because a reader outside this module has to act on it and `useSyncExternalStore` hands a component exactly one value. `migrateLegacy` sets it, `setUnitPrefs` clears it (an explicit write is a choice), `coerceStored` clears it (only `setUnitPrefs` ever wrote a set to this key), and `setShowBothUnits` preserves it across the modifier-only write it already withheld the set from. NO PERSISTENCE BEHAVIOUR CHANGED: the flag is not written to `localStorage` and `persist` still stores `units` plus `show_both_units` only. Four now-false prose claims in the file were corrected in the same commit: the header's 'all three keys are write-once history now, which makes a presence guard merely wrong rather than catastrophic' (it reasons about an ABSENT key and misses the PRESENT-but-frozen one), the same paragraph's account of why migration ignores the gallon key, and `migrateLegacy`'s two sentences listing 'any instance whose admin later switches the published flavour' as permanently unfixable and claiming non-persistence reproduced the old server-following behaviour. `utils/__tests__/unitPrefsStore.test.ts` pins the flag in both directions and across the modifier write; both mutations (migrate flags false, setUnitPrefs flags true) were run and each killed the cases naming it. 2026-09-23 (cleanup): comment only (the keyed storage event); the key test itself is unchanged.
